title: CSS Beautifier: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [CSS Beautifier](/css-beautifier) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Format compressed or messy CSS into clean, indented stylesheets. Enter your CSS code and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Format compressed or messy CSS into a clean stylesheet with two-space indentation: one rule per block, one declaration per line, and media queries nested properly. Paste minified CSS from a production file, or a stylesheet you inherited, and get readable code back in one click. Everything runs in your browser — your code is never uploaded. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the CSS Beautifier

Start by typing or pasting your CSS code. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste your CSS into the editor (or use the sample).
2. Click Beautify — the formatted stylesheet appears below.
3. Copy it and paste it into your project.

## How it works

The [CSS Beautifier](/css-beautifier) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Beautifying `.card{padding:16px;border:1px solid #ddd}` produces a .card block with each declaration on its own indented line. Try the same figures in the [CSS Beautifier](/css-beautifier) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [CSS Beautifier](/css-beautifier) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What it formats

Rules, declarations, nested blocks such as @media queries, and CSS comments, which are kept on their own lines. Declaration values are spaced as `property: value`. Selectors are left exactly as written — only the layout changes.

## What it does not do

It does not validate your CSS, remove unused rules, or change any values. A declaration that was wrong stays wrong, just easier to read. For validation, check the stylesheet against the CSS specification or your browser's developer tools.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Beautify a minified production file to understand what it does before editing it.
- Keep your source CSS readable and let a build step minify it for production.
- Comments are preserved, so notes in the original CSS survive formatting.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What does a CSS beautifier do?

It re-formats CSS with consistent indentation and line breaks — one rule per block, one declaration per line — so compressed or messy stylesheets become readable. Try it with your own numbers in the [CSS Beautifier](/css-beautifier) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does it change my CSS values?

No. Only the layout changes: spacing, indentation and line breaks. Selectors, properties and values stay exactly as written. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### Is my CSS uploaded anywhere?

No. Formatting runs entirely in your browser. Try it with your own numbers in the [CSS Beautifier](/css-beautifier) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is the CSS Beautifier free to use?

Yes. The CSS Beautifier is free to use as often as you like, with no sign-up. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [CSS Beautifier](/css-beautifier) and start straight away.
